risk_reasons: Touches worker/ — worker/jobs/OnboardingDemoWorker.ts and the worker/jobs/onboarding-demo/ helper package.

Touches src/lib/shared/logger.ts, the single emit path every worker job, poller, ingress handler and route log call reaches. A regression here is silent: wrong JSON shape, a dropped field, or a throw from a log call.
The onboarding-demo lane owns a pessimistic 20c cost-guard reservation. Losing a release path leaks daily budget; double-finalizing distorts it.
goal: Clear the two pre-existing fallow complexity findings named in issue #616 by decomposition, not suppression: logger.ts emit (cognitive 24) and OnboardingDemoWorker.ts handleOnboardingDemo (cognitive 25, CRAP 50.7 at 55.6% coverage). Both must end with zero fallow health findings while every observable behavior stays byte-identical.
non_goals: No behavior change of any kind: identical JSON log lines (same keys, same key order, same values), identical demo lifecycle transitions, identical Sentry messages, tags and levels, identical thrown errors.
No inline fallow-ignore pragma and no .fallowrc.jsonc health.ignore entry for either function — the owner rejected suppression; decomposition is the deliverable.
No public API change to createWorkerLogger, toError or logUnhandledPollError.
No schema change, no migration, no feature flag, no env var.
No change to the cost-guard reserve/finalize arithmetic, the 50/90/100 threshold set, or the pessimistic 20c reserve.
Not touching the other 18 functions fallow health reports above threshold across the repo — this run closes #616 only.
Not promoting .github/workflows/fallow.yml to a required status check — issue #616 raises that question; it is a separate decision and a separate PR.
No new top-level directory: logger helpers stay module-private inside logger.ts, worker helpers land in the existing worker/jobs/onboarding-demo/ package.
user_visible_behavior: None. Owners, admins and operators see no difference. The acceptance test is that every existing unit test stays green without modification, and that a log line emitted before the change is byte-identical to one emitted after.
invariants: Invariant #15: every extracted worker helper receives its DB client as an explicit sql parameter. worker/jobs/onboarding-demo/subscription-guard.ts must NOT import src/lib/db/server — OnboardingDemoWorker.ts is the composition root and passes sql down.
Invariant #12: entry points orchestrate; modules own failure behavior. handleOnboardingDemo keeps the orchestration order and each extracted module keeps its own try/catch posture.

Logging contract (CLAUDE.md, Tech stack): one JSON object per line; object args pass through sanitizeAnalyticsProperties; string args are logged verbatim. Extraction must not move any arg class across that boundary.

Logger fail-open contract: a log call NEVER throws. Both fail-open catches survive extraction — the per-arg sanitizer catch (data = { unserializable: true }) and the record-level JSON.stringify catch ({ message, unserializable: true }).

JSON key order contract: timestamp, level, service, logger, message, then context fields in CONTEXT_FIELDS order, then correlation_id when only the factory supplied it, then error fields in arrival order, then data last. Collecting error fields during the loop and merging them after must reproduce this exactly, because record.message is seeded early and re-assignment does not move a key.
Error-arg precedence: arg instanceof Error is tested BEFORE arg && typeof arg === 'object'. A null arg falls through both and is dropped. Later Error args overwrite earlier error_* fields.
Stack-suppression contract (#611): serializeError omits error_stack whenever requiresProductionConfig() is true, not when NODE_ENV says production.

Cost-guard reservation contract (NARROWED after plan round 1 finding F4 — the original blanket 'every path' wording did not describe the code). As built: the three terminal claim outcomes (not_found, already_terminal, race_lost) release the 20c reserve exactly once, and so do both terminal-failure paths. 'reset_to_queued' deliberately does NOT release, because the demo re-runs on the same reserve. A rejection BEFORE or DURING the claim (the subscription SELECT, claimDemo itself) and a rejected markOutboxCompleted also do NOT release, because those calls sit outside the outer try. That is existing behavior this refactor preserves and must not 'fix'. The success path finalizes actual spend and never also releases.

finalizeOnboardingDemoCost is NOT idempotent: it applies delta = actualCostCents - RESERVATION_CENTS on every call (src/lib/costs/onboarding-demo-cost-guard.ts:86). Calling it twice on one demo corrupts the daily counter, so the success path must finalize exactly once and must never also release.

Re-throw contract: failOnboardingDemoTerminal re-throws when the failure record itself cannot be written, and the reservation is released first (try/finally). Any wrapper must preserve both the release and the re-throw.
Best-effort contract: cost finalization and the threshold/Sentry block run AFTER completeDemo and must never propagate into the outer catch, which would flip a completed demo row to failed.
Mock-leak guard (#611) fires before any other work: isMockMode() && requiresProductionConfig() throws, naming the lane.
edge_cases: logger: the record-level JSON.stringify catch is NOT reachable through an object arg (corrected after plan round 1). sanitizeAnalyticsProperties (src/lib/analytics/events.ts:111-128) copies only string/number/boolean/null, so a BigInt is dropped before it reaches the record, and LogContext (src/lib/shared/log-context.ts:7-17) is all-optional-string. The only reachable trigger is an Error whose name/message/stack is non-serializable, e.g. Object.defineProperty(err, 'message', { value: 10n }). The fallback line then carries message and unserializable: true and nothing else.

logger: a circular object arg makes sanitizeAnalyticsProperties throw inside the loop. data becomes { unserializable: true } merged with whatever earlier object args contributed, and the rest of the record is intact.
logger: both a bound context correlation_id and a factory correlationId are present. The bound context wins — the factory value is applied ONLY when record.correlation_id is still undefined.

logger: number and boolean args join the message; null, undefined, symbols and functions are dropped entirely. false and 0 must still appear as 'false' and '0', so the check is typeof, never truthiness.
logger: an empty args array yields message: '' and no data key. An object arg that sanitizes to {} yields no data key either (the Object.keys length test).

worker: the onboarding_demos JOIN returns no row (demo deleted, or business/account gone). biz is undefined, the guard does NOT fire, and the job proceeds to claimDemo, which then reports not_found. The extracted guard must return 'not handled' on a missing row, not fail the demo.
worker: claimDemo returns reset_to_queued. handleOnboardingDemo THROWS so BullMQ re-dispatches, and the reservation is deliberately NOT released — the demo will run again on the same reserve.
worker: claimDemo returns not_found | already_terminal | race_lost. The outbox row is completed and the reservation IS released.
worker: reservationDate is undefined (a demo enqueued before the cost guard, or a replay). Every finalize and release call becomes a no-op; nothing may throw.
worker: completeDemo succeeds but finalizeOnboardingDemoCost throws. The error is logged and swallowed; the demo stays completed.
worker: checkCostThreshold or Sentry.captureMessage throws. Logged and swallowed; the demo stays completed and the outer catch never runs.
worker: checkCostThreshold returns several crossed thresholds. One Sentry message per threshold, level 'error' at 100, 'warning' at 90, 'info' at 50, with tags lane and threshold.

fallow: `pnpm ci:fallow` uses --gate new-only, which fails only on findings ATTRIBUTED AS INTRODUCED against origin/main. Both #616 findings are inherited, so ci:fallow passes whether or not the refactor lands. It is a regression check, never proof — the targeted fallow health assertion in verification_commands is the proof.

fallow: `fallow health` exits 1 on ANY project finding and takes no path scoping flag, so it can only be used through the JSON-plus-node-assertion form. Calling it bare in a gate makes the gate permanently red.

fallow: the checked-in coverage/coverage-final.json is stale (2026-09-11). CRAP is computed from it, so the 50.7 figure must be re-derived against coverage regenerated by the review gate before the branch claims the CRAP finding cleared.

fallow thresholds in force are the defaults, not overrides: a finding fires above cognitive 15, above cyclomatic 20, and at CRAP 30 or more. Clearing cognitive 25 means reaching 15 or below, not merely 'lower'.

verification_commands: npx fallow health --complexity --format json > .feature/fallow-health.json 2>/dev/null || true; node -e "const f=require('./.feature/fallow-health.json').findings.filter(x=>x.path.includes('src/lib/shared/logger.ts')||x.path.includes('worker/jobs/OnboardingDemoWorker.ts')||x.path.includes('worker/jobs/onboarding-demo/')); if(f.length){console.error('FAIL: complexity findings remain: '+f.map(x=>x.path+' '+x.name+':'+x.line+' cyc='+x.cyclomatic+' cog='+x.cognitive+' crap='+x.crap+' exceeded='+x.exceeded).join(' | ')); process.exit(1);} console.log('PASS: issue 616 functions and their new helpers are complexity-clear');"
rollback_plan: No schema change, no migration, no flag, no env var, no dependency. Rollback is a straight revert of the squash-merge commit on main; nothing to un-apply on either Supabase project. The staging ride precedes the prod merge, so a broken log shape or a broken demo lane surfaces on staging first. If the logger regresses after promotion, revert restores the exact prior emit body — there is no forward-fix window to manage because no state was written in a new shape.
observability: Every structured log line keeps its exact key set and key order. A staging diff of one captured worker line before and after the branch is the proof; a reordered or missing key means the emit decomposition changed the record assembly.
The '[OnboardingDemoWorker]' completion line keeps its exact text: 'Onboarding demo <id> completed (<source>): <n>/<m> responses'.
The onboarding_demo_cost_threshold_<t> Sentry messages keep level (error at 100, warning at 90, info at 50) and tags { lane: 'onboarding-demo', threshold: '<t>' }.

Staging smoke: run one onboarding demo end to end. The onboarding_demos row reaches completed with non-empty reviews and responses, the daily onboarding-demo cost counter moves by actual spend rather than the 20c reserve, and the worker log carries the completion line above.
Staging negative smoke: a demo whose account is no longer pending_payment ends failed with subscription_state_changed and the daily counter returns to its pre-reserve value.
